messages.subject: Autocalibration questions
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr Van Hees,

To analyze accelerometer data from a wrist-worn Actigraph, we are currently using your package GGIR.

We have some questions concerning the autocalibration that we hope you could answer.

1.      1) Downweighting outliers: in your paper “Autocalibration of free-living accelerometer data (2014)” the procedure of the downweighting of outliers is described as follows: “the weighting was calculated as 1-g divided by the absolute difference between the Euclidean norm corresponding to a 10-s calibration window (1 point on the ellipsoid) and 1 g with 100 being the maximum weighting.” However, we could only find this calculation in the g.calibrate function (row 438): “weights = pmin(1/sqrt(rowSums((curr-closestpoint)^2)), 1/0.01)”.

We weren’t able to figure out the mathematical approach behind this equation and the connection to the definition above. Is there maybe an additional definition of the weighting process? Could you explain the structure of this weighting definition?

2.      2) Population of the sphere: to ensure a sufficiently populated ellipsoid, you added a “sparseness criteria of at least one ellipsoid value higher than 300 mg and at least one value lower than -300 mg for each of the three axes”. Why did you choose a threshold value of +- 300 mg?

Thank you very much for your time!

Best regards,

Eric Besenius, Anne Backes

messages.body_plain:
Hi Christopher,
You are on the right path. The exported files are what you need, but I seem to have forgotten to document what those levels refer to.
I have now created an issue for it: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/107
For the time being:

0 = Sleep period time + sleep
1 = Sleep period time + wakefulness (minimal movement)
2 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + light activity
3 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + moderate activity
4 = Sleep period time + wakefulness + vigorous activity
5 = Daytime + sustained inactivity
6 = Daytime + other inactivity
7 = Daytime + light activity
8 = Daytime + moderate activity
9 = Daytime + vigorous activity
If you use three bout duration for MVPA, inactive, and light bouts then levels 10 to 18 will look as follows:
10 = Daytime + MVPA bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
11 = Daytime + MVPA bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
12 = Daytime + MVPA bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
13 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
14 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
15 = Daytime + Inactivity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)
16 = Daytime + Light activity bout, long length (whichever length you specified)
17 = Daytime + Light activity bout, medium length (whichever length you specified)
18 = Daytime + Light activity bout, short length (whichever length you specified)

As you see the number of bout levels depends on the number of bout durations you choose in the part5.
I suppose it would be good if the meaning of all these levels is reflected in the column name.

Thanks for raising this gap in the documentation, Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

1. sqrt(rowSums((curr - closestpoint)^2)) equals the distance between the point on the ellipsoid and the closest point on the sphere with radius = 1. Objects curr and closestpoint have three columns reflecting x, y and z 10 second window averages.
Next, pmin(1/ sqrt(rowSums((curr - closestpoint)^2)), 1/0.01) evaluates whether 1 divided by that distance is less than 1 divided by 0.01. Here, 1 divided by 0.01 corresponds to the maximum weighting of 100 (1/0.01= 100) mentioned in the text. In other words the algorithm only considers distances less than 0.01 g (10 mg).

2.
I choose this threshold based on the assumption that if an accelerometer is worn for multiple days it is very likely or almost certain that it will rotate for more than 300/1000 ratio of 90 degrees. Simply lying down or raising an arm should already meet this criteria. So, this threshold was primarily to make the method robust against experiments where the accelerometer is left on a table for several days. The specific value of 300 was not optimized in any way but just a first guess which worked out well.

Vincent

Some general tips which are probably relevant to everyone who interacts with this list/forum:
- Check that you do not mix up GGIR output from different GGIR version, which sometimes causes problems.
- Restart R after updating a package, which is quite often the source of the problem.
- Inspect output from GGIR part 2 when you run into issues with part 4 or 5. Often the part 2 output can give a hint about why there might be a problem. For example, the measurement was too short or the sensor was not worn at all.
- If neither of the above works, try to create a minimalistic example that someone else can use to reproduce and investigate your problem. Instructions on how to ask good questions on open source software can be found elsewhere:
https://stackoverflow.com/help/how-to-ask
https://www.biostars.org/p/75548/

As I mentioned in an earlier correspondence in this group this range threshold is probably redundant because the standard deviation threshold already makes that a wide range is almost impossible.
Vincent

messages.subject: MVPA analysis in children
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!

I am analyzing data from children aged 6-17y, and the outcome of my interest is MVPA over a week. Following the Whitehall II Study reference, I would like to retain activity lasting at least 1 min for which 80% of the activity satisfied the 191.6mg threshold criteria (children).

I am aware of:
- children threshold criteria for MVPA (based on VT Hildebrand M, VAN Hees VT et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc.2014);
- the equation to calculate MVPA over a week when less than 7 valid days of data are available:
 (5xmean daily weekday MVPA time + 2x mean daily week-end MVPA time)/7 (based on Whitehall II Study Menai M, van Hees VT et al. Scientific Reports 2017)

Therefore I plan to use part 2_daysummary.csv, to sum up for a single day of MVPA.:

MVPA_E5S_B1M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B5M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr + MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T191.6_ENMO_0-24hr

Could you please let me know if this thinking is ok?
Or shall I use other data? output 5?

I have used GGIR package 1.6.0.
I used the code as follows:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="xxx",
             outputdir="xxx",
             f0=1, f1=2,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2,               ndayswindow= 4,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 0,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(),
             qwindow = c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(),
             mvpathreshold = c(191.6),
             bout.metric = 2,
             closedbout = FALSE,
             desiredtz="Europe/Warsaw",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= c(),
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = c(),
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(56.3), threshold.mod = c(191.6),  threshold.vig = c(695.8),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage =TRUE,
             viewingwindow= 1)

Thank you!
Bart Zalewski
